Charles Dickens.name: Charles Dickens
Charles Dickens.description: Charles Dickens is the author of A Christmas Carol.

Arthur Rackham.name: Arthur Rackham
Arthur Rackham.description: Arthur Rackham is the illustrator of A Christmas Carol.

J. B. Lippincott Company.name: J. B. Lippincott Company

Ebenezer Scrooge.name: Ebenezer Scrooge
Ebenezer Scrooge.description: Ebenezer Scrooge is a character in the book, described as caustic and cold, and the employer of Bob Cratchit. | A grasping, covetous old man, the surviving partner of the firm of Scrooge and Marley. | Ebenezer Scrooge is a man who is visited by the ghost of his former business partner, Jacob Marley, and is confronted with the consequences of his worldly and uncharitable life. | Ebenezer Scrooge is a man visited by the Ghost of Jacob Marley, who warns him of future hauntings by Three Spirits. | Ebenezer Scrooge is the protagonist who, after experiencing supernatural events, is perplexed by the time shown on his clock and the bell, and anticipates a ghostly visitation. | Ebenezer Scrooge is a former apprentice of Fezziwig, now an adult observing his past Christmas Eve with the Ghost of Christmas Past. | Ebenezer Scrooge is the name on the grave that Scrooge sees, revealing his own future fate if he does not change. | Ebenezer Scrooge is the central character in A Christmas Carol who undergoes a transformation and becomes a good friend, master, and man.

Bob Cratchit.name: Bob Cratchit
Bob Cratchit.description: Bob Cratchit is a clerk to Ebenezer Scrooge and the father of Tiny Tim and Peter Cratchit. | Bob Cratchit is Scrooge's clerk, who earns fifteen 'Bob' a week and lives in a four-roomed house with his family. | Bob Cratchit is the father of the Cratchit family, a loving and cheerful man who carries Tiny Tim on his shoulder and expresses disappointment when he thinks Martha is not coming for Christmas. | Bob Cratchit is the father of the Cratchit family, who prepares a hot mixture and is moved by Tiny Tim's words. | Bob Cratchit is the father of the Cratchit family, who praises the goose and pudding as exceptional. | Bob Cratchit is the father of the Cratchit family, who proposed a toast and served the hot drink from the jug. | Bob Cratchit is a kind and mild-mannered man who proposes a toast to Scrooge as the Founder of the Feast. | Bob Cratchit is the father of the Cratchit family, whose house Scrooge visits. | Bob Cratchit is the father of the Cratchit family and husband of Mrs. Cratchit. He is portrayed as a loving and grief-stricken man who has recently lost his son Tiny Tim. | Bob Cratchit is a family man and employee of Scrooge's firm, known for his cheerful disposition and deep affection for his family, especially Tiny Tim. | Bob Cratchit is a character who expresses happiness and is part of the Cratchit family. | Bob Cratchit is Scrooge's employee and the intended recipient of the turkey. | Bob Cratchit is an employee of Scrooge, who arrives late to work and is initially confronted but then receives a salary raise and support. | Bob Cratchit is a character in A Christmas Carol who is instructed by Scrooge to buy another coal-scuttle.

Tiny Tim.name: Tiny Tim
Tiny Tim.description: Tiny Tim (Tim Cratchit) is the youngest son of Bob Cratchit, a cripple. | Tiny Tim is the young son of Bob and Mrs. Cratchit, who is physically disabled and uses a crutch, supported by an iron frame. | Tiny Tim is a small crippled boy who is carried by his siblings and expresses thoughtful wishes on Christmas Day. | Tiny Tim is a young Cratchit child who, despite his frailty, enthusiastically beats on the table and cheers during the meal. | Tiny Tim is Bob Cratchit's young son, who is ill and sits close to his father, and his mortality is a concern. | Tiny Tim is the Cratchits' young son, who drinks the toast last and shows indifference to it. | Tiny Tim is a child who has a plaintive little voice and sings a song about a lost child travelling in the snow, and is a focus of Scrooge's attention. | Tiny Tim is a child of the Cratchit family, mentioned as being ill or deceased. | Tiny Tim is the young, ill child in the Cratchit family. Although not present in the scene, his memory is central, and he is remembered fondly by his family. | Tiny Tim is the young, ailing son of the Cratchit family, whose memory and gentle nature the family cherishes, and whose loss they mourn. | Tiny Tim is referenced as a spirit with a childish essence from God, indicating his death or spiritual presence. | Tiny Tim is Bob Cratchit's son, who is small in size, mentioned in comparison to the size of the turkey. | Tiny Tim is a character in A Christmas Carol who did not die, and Scrooge becomes a second father to him.

Ghost of Christmas Past.name: Ghost of Christmas Past
Ghost of Christmas Past.description: Ghost of Christmas Past is a phantom that shows things past. | The Ghost of Christmas Past is a spirit that appears to Scrooge, with a fluctuating and indistinct form, and speaks softly about Scrooge's past. | The Ghost of Christmas Past is a spirit that shows Scrooge scenes from his past, including the Fezziwig party. | The Ghost of Christmas Past is a supernatural being who shows Scrooge visions of his past, characterized by a sense of urgency as time grows short. | The Ghost of Christmas Past is a spectral figure that previously showed Scrooge visions from his past, as recalled during the music at the gathering.

Ghost of Christmas Present.name: Ghost of Christmas Present
Ghost of Christmas Present.description: Ghost of Christmas Present is a spirit of a kind, generous, and hearty nature. | A spirit of a kind, generous, and hearty nature. | The Ghost of Christmas Present is a jolly spirit dressed in a green robe with white fur, barefoot, wearing a holly wreath, and carrying a torch. It introduces itself to Scrooge and offers to teach him lessons. | The Ghost of Christmas Present is a spectral figure, implied to be aware of the game's deception involving Topper and Scrooge's nephew.

Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come.name: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come
Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come.description: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come is an apparition showing the shadows of things which may happen. | An apparition showing the shadows of things which yet may happen. | The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come is a spectral figure that guides Scrooge through future scenes, including a churchyard.

Ghost of Jacob Marley.name: Ghost of Jacob Marley
Ghost of Jacob Marley.description: A spectre of Scrooge's former partner in business. | The ghost of Jacob Marley, a deceased business partner of Scrooge, appears to warn him and mention the Three Spirits.

Joe.name: Joe
Joe.description: A marine-store dealer and receiver of stolen goods. | Joe is a character who questions a woman about taking down bed-curtains from a deceased person's room. | Joe, referred to as old Joe, is a buyer who appraises and purchases the plundered items.

Dick Wilkins.name: Dick Wilkins
Dick Wilkins.description: A fellow apprentice of Scrooge's. | Dick Wilkins is Scrooge's fellow apprentice who was very much attached to Scrooge.

Belle.name: Belle
Belle.description: A comely matron, an old sweetheart of Scrooge's. | Belle is the wife of an old friend of Scrooge, who recognizes him and mentions his lonely state.

Caroline.name: Caroline
Caroline.description: Wife of one of Scrooge's debtors. | Caroline is a woman who receives news of the Dead Man's death with relief and hope for her family. | Caroline is a woman who expresses relief and thankfulness upon hearing of a man's death.

Mrs. Cratchit.name: Mrs. Cratchit
Mrs. Cratchit.description: Wife of Bob Cratchit. | Mrs. Cratchit is Bob's wife, who dresses in a twice-turned gown with ribbons and prepares the meal. | Mrs. Cratchit is the mother of the Cratchit family, who lovingly welcomes Martha and manages the household with warmth. | Mrs. Cratchit is the mother of the Cratchit family, who prepares the goose and asks about Tiny Tim's behavior. | Mrs. Cratchit is the matriarch of the Cratchit family, who prepared and served the Christmas goose and pudding. | Mrs. Cratchit is a member of the Cratchit family, who prepared the pudding and had doubts about the quantity of flour. | Mrs. Cratchit is Bob Cratchit's wife, who expresses strong disapproval of Scrooge and drinks to his health only for her husband's sake. | Mrs. Cratchit is the wife of Bob Cratchit and the mother of their children. She is industrious and cares for her family's well-being, especially concerned about Tiny Tim's health. | Mrs. Cratchit is Bob's wife, a loving mother who works alongside her daughters and expresses gratitude and warmth towards their benefactor. | Mrs. Cratchit is a character who kisses Bob Cratchit in a moment of family affection.

Belinda Cratchit.name: Belinda Cratchit
Belinda Cratchit.description: Daughter of Mrs. Cratchit. | Belinda Cratchit is the second daughter of Bob and Mrs. Cratchit, assisting with setting the table.

Martha Cratchit.name: Martha Cratchit
Martha Cratchit.description: Daughter of Mrs. Cratchit. | Martha Cratchit is the eldest daughter of the Cratchit family, who arrives late from work and participates in the family's Christmas activities. | Martha Cratchit is a young woman who comes from behind a closet door and runs into Bob Cratchit's arms. | Martha Cratchit is a poor apprentice at a milliner's who describes her work and plans to rest on the holiday.

Mrs. Dilber.name: Mrs. Dilber
Mrs. Dilber.description: A laundress. | Mrs. Dilber is a laundress who participates in the plundering of a deceased man's belongings.

Fan.name: Fan
Fan.description: The sister of Scrooge. | Fan is Scrooge's younger sister who brings him home from school, expressing her joy and describing their father's improved behavior.

Mrs. Fezziwig.name: Mrs. Fezziwig
Mrs. Fezziwig.description: The worthy partner of Mr. Fezziwig. | Mrs. Fezziwig is Fezziwig's wife, described as a vast substantial smile at the party. | Mrs. Fezziwig is Old Fezziwig's partner in dancing, participating in the festivities and dancing with him. | Mrs. Fezziwig is Fezziwig's wife who, alongside her husband, hosts the domestic ball and wishes guests a Merry Christmas.

Marley, who signed the register of Marley's burial and is the sole executor and mourner, known for his business acumen and lack of sentimental response to Marley's death. | Scrooge is a miserly, cold-hearted old man who is the owner of the counting-house and is known for his tight-fistedness and lack of warmth. | Scrooge is the owner of a counting-house, known for his miserly and cold demeanor, who regards Christmas as a humbug. | Scrooge is a miserly old man who expresses disdain for Christmas and is stern towards his nephew and clerk. | Scrooge is a miserly and cold-hearted man who dismisses Christmas cheer and is visited by his nephew and charity collectors. | Scrooge is the main character, a miserly man who rejects pleas to donate to the poor at Christmas. | Scrooge is a main character who is occupied with his work, resents interference, and displays a facetious temper. | Scrooge is a businessman who is grumpy and miserly, working in a counting-house and being who is being guided by the Ghost, asking questions about the places they visit. | Scrooge is the protagonist, a man who is being guided by the Ghost and is surprised to hear his nephew's laugh. | Scrooge is an old man described as comical and not very pleasant, whose wealth is of no use to him. Scrooge is the protagonist witnessing scenes of death and reflecting on his own potential fate. | Scrooge is a character who witnesses a death scene and converses with a ghost, feeling fear and regret. | Scrooge is a character who witnesses scenes of death and family life, prompted by the Ghost. | Scrooge is a miserly employer, but his nephew's kindness indirectly reflects on him in this context. | Scrooge is a character who is shown future visions and questions the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come. | Scrooge is a man who experiences a profound transformation, pledging to change his life after visions of his own grave. | Scrooge is a man who has just experienced a transformation, expressing joy and good intentions, and is interacting with the spirits and his surroundings. | engaging in charitable and kind acts, such as buying a turkey and apologizing to a gentleman. | Scrooge is a character who, after a change of heart, makes amends by giving money, visiting his nephew, and spreading kindness. | Scrooge is a central character known for his miserly behavior, but here he transforms and promises to raise Bob's salary and assist his family.

The Woman.name: The Woman
The Woman.description: The Woman is a character who admits to taking down bed-curtains with rings and all, showing a lack of reverence for the deceased. | The Woman is a character who argues for the right to take care of oneself and participates in the plunder. | A woman who laughs at the dead man's misfortune, highlighting the theme of profit from death.

Fred.name: Fred
Fred.description: Fred is Scrooge's nephew, whom Scrooge asks for entry to dinner. | Fred is Scrooge's nephew, who, despite pity for his uncle, maintains good humor and intends to visit Scrooge every year to wish him well. | Fred is Scrooge's nephew who instigates the guessing game and proposes a toast to Uncle Scrooge. | Fred is Scrooge's nephew, who welcomes Scrooge into his home for dinner. | Fred is a character who comes to dinner and is warmly welcomed, indicating a positive relationship with the host.

Old Scratch.name: Old Scratch
Old Scratch.description: Old Scratch is a colloquial name for the devil, referred to by one character in regard to someone getting what they deserved.

Bed-Curtains.name: Bed-Curtains
Bed-Curtains.description: Bed-curtains are fabric hangings around a bed, which the woman took down despite the occupant being deceased.

Illustration List.name: Illustration List
Illustration List.description: A list of black and white illustrations with page numbers, including tailpieces, headings, and descriptions of scenes from the text.

Marley.name: Marley
Marley.description: Marley is Scrooge's deceased business partner, whose death is confirmed without doubt and whose name remains on the warehouse door years after. | Marley is the business partner of Scrooge in the firm Scrooge and Marley. | Marley is Scrooge's deceased business partner, dead for seven years, whose ghostly face appears on the door knocker. | Marley is a deceased associate of Scrooge, whose pigtail Scrooge half-expects to see when he checks behind the door. | Marley is a deceased individual, seven years dead, whose face haunts Scrooge's thoughts. | Marley is a person referred to in the text, apparently a previous occupant or associate of the building, and whose time is mentioned in comparison to Scrooge's.

Scrooge and Marley.name: Scrooge and Marley
Scrooge and Marley.description: Scrooge and Marley is the firm name above the warehouse door, indicating the partnership that continued to bear Marley's name after his death. | Scrooge and Marley is the firm owned by Scrooge and Marley, known for its counting-house.

Marley's Ghost.name: Marley's Ghost
Marley's Ghost.description: Marley's Ghost is the title of the first stave, indicating the supernatural visitation that is pivotal to the story. | Marley's Ghost is the supernatural manifestation of Marley, appearing as a face on the door knocker with a dismal light and ghostly spectacles. | Marley's Ghost is the specter of Jacob Marley, Scrooge's former business partner, who appears to Scrooge wrapped in chains and seeking to communicate. | Marley's Ghost is a spectral figure whose chains are worn by other phantoms, indicating a shared condition of being bound. | Marley's Ghost is the ghost of Scrooge's former business partner, whose appearance and warning about a future visitation trouble Scrooge's mind.

Counting-House.name: Counting-House
Counting-House.description: The counting-house is the office where Scrooge conducts his business.

The Clerk.name: The Clerk
The Clerk.description: The clerk works for Scrooge in a small, dismal cell, copying letters, and has a very small fire that he cannot replenish. | The clerk is Scrooge's employee who receives Christmas greetings from the nephew and returns them warmly, contrasting with Scrooge's coldness. | The clerk is an employee in Scrooge's counting-house who is overworked and underappreciated, but cheerful on Christmas Eve.

Scrooge's Nephew.name: Scrooge's Nephew
Scrooge's Nephew.description: Scrooge's nephew is a cheerful, healthy man who visits Scrooge to wish him a merry Christmas, despite Scrooge's negativity. | Scrooge's nephew is a kind and cheerful man who defends Christmas and invites Scrooge to dine with him. | Scrooge's nephew is a cheerful and persistent man who invites Scrooge to dine and tries to maintain a friendly relationship despite rejection. | Scrooge's nephew, who laughs heartily in a bright room and is approved of by the Spirit. | Scrooge's nephew, named Fred, is a cheerful and good-humored man who laughs heartily and defends his uncle despite Scrooge's grumpy nature. | Scrooge's nephew is a relative who hosts the family gathering and is involved in the arrangement of the blind man's-buff game with Topper. | Scrooge's nephew is the host of the party and participates in the games, thinking of an animal in the game Yes and No.

Counting-house.name: Counting-house
Counting-house.description: The counting-house is Scrooge's place of business, where he works and keeps his clerk, and where the initial scene takes place.

Fog.name: Fog
Fog.description: The fog is a dense, cold atmospheric condition that pervades the environment outside and seeps into the counting-house.

Fire.name: Fire
Fire.description: There are small fires in the counting-house; Scrooge's fire is small, and the clerk's fire is even smaller, consisting of one coal.

Coal-box.name: Coal-box
Coal-box.description: The coal-box is kept in Scrooge's room, preventing the clerk from replenishing his fire.

Candle.name: Candle
Candle.description: The candle is used by the clerk in an attempt to warm himself, though he fails due to lack of imagination.

Scrooge's Clerk.name: Scrooge's Clerk
Scrooge's Clerk.description: Scrooge's clerk is an employee who secretly shows approval of the nephew's views but is scolded by Scrooge.

Christmas.name: Christmas
Christmas.description: Christmas is a holiday that Scrooge despises but his nephew regards as a time for kindness and charity. | Christmas is the festive season during which the gentlemen seek donations for the poor. | Christmas is the holiday being celebrated, and the Ghost spreads its spirit. | The holiday of Christmas is central to the scenes depicted, with the two men and ship crew celebrating it. | Christmas is a holiday that Scrooge's nephew mentions as being called a humbug by Scrooge. | Christmas is the festive occasion during which the family gathering occurs, noted for the theme of childhood and the birth of its Founder. | Christmas is the holiday period that seems to be condensed into the time Scrooge spends with the Ghost. | Christmas is a holiday theme central to the narrative, associated with generosity and goodwill. | Christmas is an annual holiday that Scrooge learns to keep well, and it is central to the narrative.

Mr. Marley.name: Mr. Marley
Mr. Marley.description: Mr. Marley is Scrooge's former business partner who has been dead for seven years.

The Portly Gentlemen.name: The Portly Gentlemen
The Portly Gentlemen.description: The portly gentlemen are charity collectors with books and papers who approach Scrooge for donations, referencing his business name.

Scrooge and Marley's.name: Scrooge and Marley's
Scrooge and Marley's.description: Scrooge and Marley's is the business firm run by Scrooge and formerly Marley, mentioned by the charity collectors.

Gentleman.name: Gentleman
Gentleman.description: The Gentleman is one of two portly gentlemen who visit Scrooge to raise funds for the poor at Christmas.

Prisons.name: Prisons
Prisons.description: Prisons are institutions that Scrooge refers to as a means of supporting the poor.

Union Workhouses.name: Union Workhouses
Union Workhouses.description: Union workhouses are facilities that Scrooge mentions as existing for the poor.

Treadmill.name: Treadmill
Treadmill.description: The Treadmill is a penal device that Scrooge references as being in full operation.

Poor Law.name: Poor Law
Poor Law.description: The Poor Law is legislation that Scrooge mentions as being in full vigour.

The Poor.name: The Poor
The Poor.description: The Poor are the destitute individuals the gentlemen aim to help with meat, drink, and warmth.

The Gentlemen.name: The Gentlemen
The Gentlemen.description: The Gentlemen are a group who withdraw after failing to persuade Scrooge.

The Ancient Tower.name: The Ancient Tower
The Ancient Tower.description: The ancient tower of a church becomes invisible in the fog, with its bell striking hours in the clouds.

The Lord Mayor.name: The Lord Mayor
The Lord Mayor.description: The Lord Mayor orders his household to keep Christmas in a grand manner.

The Little Tailor.name: The Little Tailor
The Little Tailor.description: The little tailor stirs pudding in his garret while his wife and baby go out to buy beef, despite being fined.

The Carol Singer.name: The Carol Singer
The Carol Singer.description: The carol singer attempts to regale Scrooge with a Christmas carol at his keyhole.

The Cold.name: The Cold
The Cold.description: The cold is intense, piercing, and biting, affecting the city and its inhabitants.

The Mansion House.name: The Mansion House
The Mansion House.description: The Mansion House is the stronghold of the Lord Mayor.

The Ragged Men and Boys.name: The Ragged Men and Boys
The Ragged Men and Boys.description: A party of ragged men and boys gather around a fire to warm themselves.

The Singer.name: The Singer
The Singer.description: The singer is a person who attempts to sing a Christmas carol at Scrooge's keyhole but is frightened away by Scrooge's reaction.

The Counting-House.name: The Counting-House
The Counting-House.description: The counting-house is Scrooge's place of business where he works and interact with his clerk. | The Counting-House is the business premises of Scrooge and Marley, where Marley's spirit never roved beyond during his life.

The Tavern.name: The Tavern
The Tavern.description: The tavern is where Scrooge takes his melancholy dinner in the evening.

The Chambers.name: The Chambers
The Chambers.description: The chambers are Scrooge's gloomy suite of rooms that once belonged to his deceased partner.

The Ruler.name: The Ruler
The Ruler.description: The ruler is an object Scrooge seizes to frighten away the carol singer.

Christmas Eve.name: Christmas Eve
Christmas Eve.description: Christmas Eve is the holiday that causes the clerk to be granted a day off and leads to various interactions.

The Christmas Carol.name: The Christmas Carol
The Christmas Carol.description: The Christmas Carol is a song sung by the singer, which Scrooge reacts to negatively.

Genius of the Weather.name: Genius of the Weather
Genius of the Weather.description: The Genius of the Weather is a metaphorical entity representing the weather, depicted as sitting in mournful meditation on the threshold of Scrooge's house.

The House.name: The House
The House.description: The house is Scrooge's residence and workplace; it is old, dreary, and dark, with a large knocker on its door. | Scrooge's house, which contains multiple rooms, a hall, stairs, and cellars, and is the setting for the scene.

The Door Knocker.name: The Door Knocker
The Door Knocker.description: The door knocker is a large, unremarkable fitting on Scrooge's front door, which temporarily transforms into Marley's face.

City of London.name: City of London
City of London.description: The City of London is the metropolitan area where Scrooge resides and works.

The Bell.name: The Bell
The Bell.description: The Bell is a disused bell in Scrooge's room that begins to swing and ring loudly, causing Scrooge astonishment and dread.

The Chain.name: The Chain
The Chain.description: The Chain is a heavy chain heard clanking below, associated with ghostly presence. | The Chain is a heavy chain made of cash-boxes, keys, padlocks, ledgers, deeds, and purses wound about Marley's Ghost, symbolizing his earthly attachments. | The Chain is a heavy, ponderous chain that the Ghost wears, which Scrooge learns was forged by Marley's own actions and represents his greed and neglect of humanity. | A heavy chain carried by the ghost, symbolizing the burdens and consequences of his earthly misdeeds.

The Dutch Merchant.name: The Dutch Merchant
The Dutch Merchant.description: The Dutch Merchant is the original builder of the old fireplace with Dutch tiles.

The Fire.name: The Fire
The Fire.description: The Fire is a low fire in the fireplace that provides little warmth on the bitter night. | The fire in the Cratchit home is used for cooking and warmth, tended by Peter Cratchit.

Jacob Marley.name: Jacob Marley
Jacob Marley.description: Jacob Marley was Scrooge's business partner in life, and now appears as a ghost to Scrooge. | Jacob Marley is the deceased former business partner of Scrooge, who appears as a ghost burdened with a heavy chain, representing his sins in life. | The ghost of Jacob Marley, a former business partner of Scrooge, who appears in chains and speaks of remorse and the importance of caring for mankind. | Jacob Marley is a deceased individual who intervened to arrange the visitation of the spirits to Scrooge. | Jacob Marley is a deceased character, referenced as being buried by the sexton's spade, whose death is connected to Scrooge's past reflections. | Jacob Marley is the deceased former partner of Scrooge, whose prediction about the coming of the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come is remembered by Scrooge. | Jacob Marley is a deceased former partner of Scrooge, whose ghost is referenced as having entered through a door in Scrooge's room.

The Fireplace.name: The Fireplace
The Fireplace.description: The Fireplace is within Scrooge's room where Marley's Ghost sits down opposite Scrooge.

The Ghost.name: The Ghost
The Ghost.description: The Ghost is a supernatural apparition that confronts Scrooge about his beliefs and demonstrates its reality through frightful actions. | The Ghost is the spectral form of Jacob Marley who visits Scrooge to warn him about the fate that awaits him if he does not change his ways. | The supernatural entity that appears to Scrooge, identified as the ghost of Jacob Marley, bound in chains and expressing regret for his past life. | The Ghost is a spectre that listens to the phantoms' lamentations and joins in their mournful dirge before floating out into the night. | The Ghost is a supernatural being that appears as a child-like figure with white hair, long muscular arms, a tunic of purest white, a lustrous belt, and a jet of light from its head. It holds a branch of fresh green holly. | The Ghost is a spirit who guides Scrooge through recollections of his past, pointing out significant scenes. | The Ghost is a supernatural being that Scrooge observes and communicates with during the narrative. | The Ghost is a spirit that accompanies Scrooge, showing him scenes from his past and questioning the significance of Fezziwig's actions. | A supernatural entity that forces Scrooge to observe scenes from the past. | The Ghost is a supernatural spirit whose light is bright and which Scrooge attempts to extinguish. | The Ghost is a supernatural character who instructs Scrooge to touch its robe, leading to a transformation of the scene. | The Ghost is a spirit that shows Scrooge the Cratchit family and reveals the potential future of Tiny Tim. | The Ghost is a supernatural being who rebukes Scrooge and guides him to observe the Cratchit family. | The Ghost is a supernatural entity that accompanies Scrooge and observes the party with him. | The Ghost (likely the Ghost of Christmas Present) is a supernatural entity that shows Scrooge scenes of various homes and refuges. | The Ghost, likely the Ghost of Christmas Present, appears to age during the night and reveals two children hidden beneath its robe. | The Ghost is a supernatural being guiding Scrooge, pointing to a head and revealing a scene of a family. | The Ghost is a supernatural entity that guides Scrooge through various scenes. | The Ghost is a spectral entity that shows Scrooge visions, including his neglected grave, and remains immovable until Scrooge's entreaties.

Mankind's Welfare.name: Mankind's Welfare
Mankind's Welfare.description: The ideal that charity, mercy, forbearance, and benevolence should be one's primary business, as emphasized by the ghost.

Christian Spirit.name: Christian Spirit
Christian Spirit.description: The notion of a spirit working kindly in its sphere, serving as a moral ideal for mortals.

The Three Spirits.name: The Three Spirits
The Three Spirits.description: The Three Spirits are supernatural beings that will visit Scrooge to give him a chance to escape Marley's fate.

The Phantoms.name: The Phantoms
The Phantoms.description: The phantoms are wandering spirits in the air, each wearing chains like Marley's Ghost, and they express sorrow and regret over lost opportunities to do good.

The Old Ghost in a White Waistcoat.name: The Old Ghost in a White Waistcoat
The Old Ghost in a White Waistcoat.description: This ghost is an elderly spirit, recognizable to Scrooge, who is burdened by an iron safe and cries at his inability to help a woman and infant on a doorstep.

The Invisible World.name: The Invisible World
The Invisible World.description: The Invisible World represents the supernatural realm that Scrooge glimpses, which contributes to his emotional state and need for rest.

The Church Bell.name: The Church Bell
The Church Bell.description: The church bell is the clock in the neighboring church that strikes the quarters and then rings up to twelve, marking the time for Scrooge.

Scrooge's Repeater.name: Scrooge's Repeater
Scrooge's Repeater.description: Scrooge's repeater is a pocket watch that he uses to check the time, but it also strikes twelve, adding to his confusion about the actual time.

The Clock.name: The Clock
The Clock.description: The heavy bell and clock in Scrooge's residence ring from six to twelve and then stop, leading Scrooge to suspect an icicle interfering with the works.

The First of Exchange.name: The First of Exchange
The First of Exchange.description: A financial document mentioning Mr. Ebenezer Scrooge, referenced in the text as part of Scrooge's thoughts about counting days.

The Visitation.name: The Visitation
The Visitation.description: The predicted supernatural visitation that Marley's Ghost warned Scrooge about, expected when the bell tolls one.

The Hour Bell.name: The Hour Bell
The Hour Bell.description: The hour bell is a bell that chimes the hours and signals the arrival of the supernatural visitor.

Spirit.name: Spirit
Spirit.description: The Spirit is a supernatural entity that leads Scrooge through time, taking him to a past winter day on an open country road. | A supernatural being that carries a torch and sprinkles drops on dinners, engaging in dialogue with Scrooge. | The Spirit is another supernatural entity that stands by Scrooge and looks approvingly at the nephew. | The Spirit is a supernatural figure standing by Scrooge's side, observing the scene with approving affability. | A phantom ghost that guides the protagonist through the future, observing conversations and scenes.

Country Road.name: Country Road
Country Road.description: A country road with fields on either hand, representing the rural area where Scrooge grew up, now covered in snow.

Market Town.name: Market Town
Market Town.description: A small market-town in the distance with a bridge, church, and winding river, associated with Scrooge's childhood memories.

Boys.name: Boys
Boys.description: Boys riding shaggy ponies or in gigs and carts, depicted as joyful and full of spirits, calling to each other and exchanging Christmas greetings.

Farmers.name: Farmers
Farmers.description: Farmers who drive the country gigs and carts, part of the scene of Scrooge's past.

The School.name: The School
The School.description: The School is a neglected building in Scrooge's past, where he was left alone during Christmas as a child.

Ali Baba.name: Ali Baba
Ali Baba.description: Ali Baba is a fictional character from a story, who appears as a vision to Scrooge, representing a source of comfort and imagination for his younger self. | A character from the story of Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves, seen by Scrooge as a figure from his past, appearing with an axe and an ass laden with wood.

The Boy (Scrooge as a child).name: The Boy (Scrooge as a child)
The Boy (Scrooge as a child).description: The Boy is a young Scrooge, left alone at school, neglected by friends, and reading near a fire.

Valentine.name: Valentine
Valentine.description: A character from a story, referred to as Valentine, with a wild brother named Orson.

Orson.name: Orson
Orson.description: The wild brother of Valentine in a story, mentioned by Scrooge.

Sultan's Groom.name: Sultan's Groom
Sultan's Groom.description: A character who was turned upside down by the Genii, mentioned by Scrooge.

Genii.name: Genii
Genii.description: Mythical beings who turned the Sultan's Groom upside down.

Princess.name: Princess
Princess.description: The Princess to whom the Sultan's Groom was married, as mentioned by Scrooge.

Parrot.name: Parrot
Parrot.description: A parrot with a green body and yellow tail that Scrooge recalls from a story, associated with Robin Crusoe.

Robin Crusoe.name: Robin Crusoe
Robin Crusoe.description: A character from the story of Robinson Crusoe, who kept a parrot named 'Poor Robin Crusoe'.

Friday.name: Friday
Friday.description: A character from the story of Robinson Crusoe, running for his life to a creek.

The Spirit.name: The Spirit
The Spirit.description: The Ghost of Christmas Past, who is showing Scrooge visions of his past Christmases. | The Spirit is a supernatural being, likely the Ghost of Christmas Present, who engages in dialogue with Scrooge and demonstrates the ability to fit into any space. | The Spirit is a supernatural entity accompanying Scrooge, exulting in the warmth and gatherings of the homes they pass. | The Spirit, also known as the Ghost of Christmas Present, shows Scrooge the children Ignorance and Want, and warns about the boy Ignorance. | The Spirit is a phantom-like entity that guides Scrooge through various scenes, pointing out meetings and conversations.

The Boy Singing Carol.name: The Boy Singing Carol
The Boy Singing Carol.description: A boy who was singing a Christmas carol at Scrooge's door the previous night, mentioned by Scrooge.

The Schoolmaster.name: The Schoolmaster
The Schoolmaster.description: The Schoolmaster is a person at the school who announces Scrooge's box, glares at him, and hosts a farewell gathering with wine and cake.

Scrooge's Box.name: Scrooge's Box
Scrooge's Box.description: Scrooge's Box is a container that is brought down at the school and likely holds Scrooge's belongings for his departure.

School Setting.name: School Setting
School Setting.description: The school is the location where Scrooge is staying and is visited by Fan; it is also where the schoolmaster appears.

The Parlour.name: The Parlour
The Parlour.description: The parlour is a cold room in the school where the schoolmaster entertains the children with wine and cake.

Master Scrooge.name: Master Scrooge
Master Scrooge.description: Master Scrooge is a young boy who is a student at the school and is leaving it in a chaise.

Schoolmaster.name: Schoolmaster
Schoolmaster.description: The schoolmaster is the person who produces the wine and cake and bids the children goodbye.

Ghost.name: Ghost
Ghost.description: The Ghost is a supernatural being that accompanies Scrooge and shows him scenes from his past, including his time at school and his apprenticeship at Fezziwig's warehouse. | The Ghost is a supernatural being showing Scrooge shadows of the past, embodying various faces. | The Ghost is a supernatural being that travels with Scrooge, showing him various scenes, including a miner's hut and the sea. | The Ghost is a spectral entity that leads Scrooge on a journey across time and space, showing him scenes of Christmas in various locations.

Old Fezziwig.name: Old Fezziwig
Old Fezziwig.description: Old Fezziwig is a cheerful gentleman who runs a warehouse where Scrooge was apprenticed. | Old Fezziwig is a host of a festive dance event, leading the dancing and interacting with guests, showing energetic and joyful behavior.

Postboy.name: Postboy
Postboy.description: The postboy is a servant who is offered a glass of 'something' by the schoolmaster's servant but declines.

Decanter of Light Wine.name: Decanter of Light Wine
Decanter of Light Wine.description: A decanter containing curiously light wine, produced by the schoolmaster.

Block of Heavy Cake.name: Block of Heavy Cake
Block of Heavy Cake.description: A block of curiously heavy cake, produced by the schoolmaster.

Warehouse.name: Warehouse
Warehouse.description: The warehouse where Scrooge was apprenticed to Fezziwig. | The warehouse is Fezziwig's place of business that is transformed into a ballroom for the Christmas Eve party.

School.name: School
School.description: The school from which Master Scrooge departs at the beginning of the scene.

Fezziwig.name: Fezziwig
Fezziwig.description: Fezziwig is a jovial and energetic employer who hosts a Christmas Eve party in his warehouse for his employees and others. | Fezziwig is a character who hosts a domestic ball and is praised by his apprentices for making them happy through his kind words and looks.

Three Miss Fezziwigs.name: Three Miss Fezziwigs
Three Miss Fezziwigs.description: The Three Miss Fezziwigs are the daughters of Fezziwig, who are beaming and lovable at the party.

Fiddler.name: Fiddler
Fiddler.description: The fiddler is a musician who provides music for the party, tuning his instrument. | The fiddler is a musician playing for the dance, who plays energetically and even resumes playing without rest.

Party Attendees.name: Party Attendees
Party Attendees.description: Various employees and local people attend the Fezziwig Christmas party, including the housemaid, cook, and others.

Dance Event.name: Dance Event
Dance Event.description: A social gathering featuring various dances, music, and refreshments like cake and roast.

Sir Roger de Coverley.name: Sir Roger de Coverley
Sir Roger de Coverley.description: A dance tune played by the fiddler, prompting the main dance of the evening.

Negus.name: Negus
Negus.description: A warm spiced wine beverage served at the dance event.

Cold Roast.name: Cold Roast
Cold Roast.description: A dish of roasted meat, served cold, at the dance event.

Cold Boiled.name: Cold Boiled
Cold Boiled.description: A dish of boiled meat, served cold, at the dance event.

Mince-Pies.name: Mince-Pies
Mince-Pies.description: Sweet pastries filled with mincemeat, served at the dance event.

Dick.name: Dick
Dick.description: Dick is a former apprentice who, along with Scrooge, participates in the ball and later praises Fezziwig.

The Two Apprentices.name: The Two Apprentices
The Two Apprentices.description: The two apprentices are former workers at Fezziwig's establishment who pour out their hearts in praise of Fezziwig.

The Domestic Ball.name: The Domestic Ball
The Domestic Ball.description: The domestic ball is a festive gathering hosted by Fezziwig and his wife, featuring dancing and ending with Christmas well-wishes.

Young Girl.name: Young Girl
Young Girl.description: A fair young girl in mourning dress who confronts Scrooge's former self about how his pursuit of wealth has displaced their relationship. | A beautiful young girl sitting near the fire, who resembles a figure from Scrooge's past, participating in the family's joyful activities.

She.name: She
She.description: The female character who releases him from their engagement, reflecting on how their relationship has changed.

He.name: He
He.description: The male character being released from the engagement, feels the justice of the supposition and struggles with it. | He is the deceased man whose belongings are being sold by the women.

The Beautiful Young Girl.name: The Beautiful Young Girl
The Beautiful Young Girl.description: A young girl who appears in the new scene, so like the previous girl that Scrooge mistakes her for the same.

Comely Matron.name: Comely Matron
Comely Matron.description: A comely matron sitting opposite her daughter, likely the mother of the young girl, laughing heartily and enjoying the children's play.

Mother.name: Mother
Mother.description: The mother is a comely matron who laughs heartily and enjoys the uproarious activities of the children.

Daughter.name: Daughter
Daughter.description: The daughter is a young girl who joins in the sports, gets playfully pillaged by the children, and greets her father's return.

Father.name: Father
Father.description: The father returns home attended by a man laden with Christmas toys and presents, and is greeted by the children.

Porter.name: Porter
Porter.description: A man laden with Christmas toys and presents who is attacked by the children in a playful manner.

Children.name: Children
Children.description: A group of more children than Scrooge can count, each behaving boisterously, engaging in playful attacks and sports.

Winter Fire.name: Winter Fire
Winter Fire.description: A fire in the room where the young girl and others are seated, providing comfort and warmth.

Room.name: Room
Room.description: A room that is not very large or handsome, but full of comfort, where the scene takes place.

Christmas Toys.name: Christmas Toys
Christmas Toys.description: Toys brought by the porter for the children as Christmas presents.

Presents.name: Presents
Presents.description: Presents brought by the porter for the children as Christmas gifts.

Master of the House.name: Master of the House
Master of the House.description: The Master of the House is a family man who is happy with his wife and daughter, and is an old friend of Scrooge.

Master's Daughter.name: Master's Daughter
Master's Daughter.description: The Master's Daughter is a graceful young girl who leans on her father affectionately, symbolizing what Scrooge could have had.

Master's Wife.name: Master's Wife
Master's Wife.description: The Master's Wife is the wife in the family scene, sitting with her daughter and husband.

Scrooge's Office.name: Scrooge's Office
Scrooge's Office.description: Scrooge's Office is the place where the Master of the House passes by and sees Scrooge sitting alone. | Scrooge's office is a place that Scrooge observes in the future, finding it occupied by someone else.

Scrooge's Partner.name: Scrooge's Partner
Scrooge's Partner.description: Scrooge's Partner is mentioned as being on the point of death, contributing to Scrooge's isolation.

The Extinguisher-Cap.name: The Extinguisher-Cap
The Extinguisher-Cap.description: The Extinguisher-Cap is an object that Scrooge uses to try to cover the Ghost's light.

The Second Spirit.name: The Second Spirit
The Second Spirit.description: The Second Spirit is the second supernatural messenger sent to Scrooge, expected to appear at One o'clock.

The Bedroom.name: The Bedroom
The Bedroom.description: The Bedroom is where Scrooge finds himself after the encounter with the Ghost and where he prepares for the Second Spirit.

Spontaneous Combustion.name: Spontaneous Combustion
Spontaneous Combustion.description: Spontaneous combustion is the frightening possibility that Scrooge briefly fears is happening to him, as he is unable to explain the strange light.

Ghostly Light.name: Ghostly Light
Ghostly Light.description: The ghostly light is a mysterious, alarming illumination that fills Scrooge's room, and which he traces to the adjoining room.

Adjoining Room.name: Adjoining Room
Adjoining Room.description: The adjoining room is where the ghostly light appears to originate, and it undergoes a surprising transformation into a grove-like space with festive decorations and food.

The Feast.name: The Feast
The Feast.description: The feast is the collection of food and drink displayed in the transformed room, including turkeys, geese, puddings, and punch, piled up to form a throne.

Plenty's Horn.name: Plenty's Horn
Plenty's Horn.description: Plenty's Horn is a symbolic torch held by the Ghost of Christmas Present, resembling the horn of plenty, and used to shed light.

Christmas Morning.name: Christmas Morning
Christmas Morning.description: Christmas Morning is the setting in which Scrooge and the Ghost find themselves after a magical transition.

City Streets.name: City Streets
City Streets.description: The city streets are the location on Christmas morning, depicted with snow, mud, and bustling activity.

Snow.name: Snow
Snow.description: Snow covers the rooftops and ground, and is cleared by people and enjoyed by boys who watch it fall.

Great Britain.name: Great Britain
Great Britain.description: Great Britain is referenced as the origin of the sooty atoms from chimneys, indicating a broader setting.

Poulterers' Shops.name: Poulterers' Shops
Poulterers' Shops.description: The poulterers' shops are still half open on Christmas morning, part of the bustling holiday scene.

Fruiterers' Shops.name: Fruiterers' Shops
Fruiterers' Shops.description: The fruiterers' shops are radiant in their glory, displaying produce like chestnuts and onions.

Chestnuts.name: Chestnuts
Chestnuts.description: Chestnuts are displayed in baskets at fruiterers' shops, described as large and pot-bellied.

Spanish Onions.name: Spanish Onions
Spanish Onions.description: Spanish onions are displayed as ruddy, brown-faced, and broad-girthed at fruiterers' shops. | Spanish onions are a type of vegetable described as ruddy, brown-faced, and broad-girthed, shining like Spanish friars, and winking at the girls from their shelves.

Girls.name: Girls
Girls.description: The girls are passerby who glance demurely at the hung-up mistletoe and are winked at by the Spanish onions.

Mistletoe.name: Mistletoe
Mistletoe.description: Mistletoe is a plant hung up in the shop, glanced at by the girls.

Pears And Apples.name: Pears And Apples
Pears And Apples.description: Pears and apples are fruits clustered high in blooming pyramids.

Grapes.name: Grapes
Grapes.description: Grapes are fruits made to dangle from conspicuous hooks to entice passersby.

Filberts.name: Filberts
Filberts.description: Filberts are nuts, mossy and brown, with a fragrance recalling ancient walks among woods.

Norfolk Biffins.name: Norfolk Biffins
Norfolk Biffins.description: Norfolk Biffins are apples, squab and swarthy, setting off the yellow of oranges and lemons, and entreating to be carried home in paper bags.

Oranges And Lemons.name: Oranges And Lemons
Oranges And Lemons.description: Oranges and lemons are citrus fruits that are yellow and set off by the Norfolk Biffins.

Gold And Silver Fish.name: Gold And Silver Fish
Gold And Silver Fish.description: Gold and silver fish are fish set forth in a bowl among choice fruits, appearing to know something is going on and gasping in excitement.

The Grocers'.name: The Grocers'
The Grocers'.description: The Grocers' is a shop nearly closed with shutters down, but with glimpses of goods and activities inside.

Scales.name: Scales
Scales.description: Scales are weighing instruments that descend on the counter making a merry sound.

Twine And Roller.name: Twine And Roller
Twine And Roller.description: Twine and roller are tools used in the grocery that part company briskly.

Canisters.name: Canisters
Canisters.description: Canisters are containers rattled up and down like juggling tricks.

Tea And Coffee.name: Tea And Coffee
Tea And Coffee.description: Tea and coffee are beverages whose blended scents are grateful to the nose.

Raisins.name: Raisins
Raisins.description: Raisins are dried grapes, plentiful and rare.

Almonds.name: Almonds
Almonds.description: Almonds are nuts that are extremely white.

Sticks Of Cinnamon.name: Sticks Of Cinnamon
Sticks Of Cinnamon.description: Sticks of cinnamon are long and straight spice sticks.

Other Spices.name: Other Spices
Other Spices.description: Other spices are described as delicious.

Candied Fruits.name: Candied Fruits
Candied Fruits.description: Candied fruits are fruits caked and spotted with molten sugar, making lookers-on feel faint.

Figs.name: Figs
Figs.description: Figs are fruit that are moist and pulpy.

Grocer.name: Grocer
Grocer.description: The grocer is a shopkeeper whose establishment is described along with the busy customers during Christmas preparations.

Bakers' Shops.name: Bakers' Shops
Bakers' Shops.description: The bakers' shops are where people carry their dinners for cooking during Christmas Day.

The Torch.name: The Torch
The Torch.description: The Spirit's torch is a special implement that sprinkles drops of water and incense on dinners, affecting their recipients' mood.

Christmas Day.name: Christmas Day
Christmas Day.description: Christmas Day is a significant holiday during which the events of the narrative occur. | Christmas Day is the holiday being celebrated by the Cratchit family, during which they enjoy a meal together. | Christmas Day is a holiday on which the Cratchits gather and exchange toasts, despite their feelings about Scrooge. | The holiday that Scrooge learns it is, prompting his joyful transformation.

Incense.name: Incense
Incense.description: Incense is a substance that the Spirit sprinkles from the torch onto dinners.

Water Drops.name: Water Drops
Water Drops.description: Water drops from the torch restore good humor to quarreling dinner-carriers.

Master Peter Cratchit.name: Master Peter Cratchit
Master Peter Cratchit.description: Master Peter Cratchit is the son and heir of Bob Cratchit, who is proudly attired in a shirt with a monstrous collar. | Master Peter Cratchit is one of the Cratchit children, who mashes potatoes and helps fetch the goose.

The Cratchit Dwelling.name: The Cratchit Dwelling
The Cratchit Dwelling.description: The Cratchit dwelling is the four-roomed house where Bob Cratchit and his family live, blessed by the Spirit's torch.

The Seventh Day.name: The Seventh Day
The Seventh Day.description: The Seventh Day refers to a weekly day of rest and dining, which Scrooge suggests is being deprived by the closing of places.

Peter Cratchit.name: Peter Cratchit
Peter Cratchit.description: Peter Cratchit is the eldest son of the Cratchit family, who is dressed in his father's shirt-collar and helps with the fire. | Peter Cratchit is the eldest son of the Cratchit family. He is attentive to his father's habits and notes that Bob has been walking slower recently. | Peter Cratchit is the eldest son of the Cratchit family, who is teased by his sisters about his future, and is the subject of a potential job offer. | Peter Cratchit is a character who shakes hands with Bob Cratchit, part of the Cratchit family.

Two Young Cratchits.name: Two Young Cratchits
Two Young Cratchits.description: Two young Cratchit children (boy and girl) are energetic and joyful, running in with news of the goose and teasing Martha. | Two young Cratchits are the younger children who help carry Tiny Tim and set chairs.

The Goose.name: The Goose
The Goose.description: The goose is a central food item for the Cratchit family's Christmas meal, cooked at the baker's and eagerly anticipated. | The Goose is the main dish of the Christmas dinner, cooked and served by the Cratchit family. | The Goose is the main dish of the Christmas dinner, celebrated for its tenderness, flavour, size, and cheapness.

The Baker's.name: The Baker's
The Baker's.description: The baker's is a shop where the Cratchit family's goose is cooked.

The Parks.name: The Parks
The Parks.description: The fashionable Parks are where Peter Cratchit yearns to show off his new shirt-collar.

Miss Belinda Cratchit.name: Miss Belinda Cratchit
Miss Belinda Cratchit.description: Miss Belinda Cratchit is one of the Cratchit children, who sweetens the apple sauce.

Belinda.name: Belinda
Belinda.description: Belinda is one of the Cratchit children who assists by changing the plates during the meal.

The Pudding.name: The Pudding
The Pudding.description: The Pudding is a dessert prepared by Mrs. Cratchit, served with ignited brandy and Christmas holly, and regarded as a great success. | The pudding is a large dessert made for the Cratchit family's Christmas dinner, considered insufficient by some but no one dared to criticize.

Christmas Dinner.name: Christmas Dinner
Christmas Dinner.description: Christmas Dinner is the festive meal shared by the Cratchit family, featuring the goose and pudding.

Cratchit Family.name: Cratchit Family
Cratchit Family.description: The Cratchit family is the household of Bob Cratchit, including Mrs. Cratchit, Tiny Tim, and other members, gathered for Christmas dinner.

Master Peter.name: Master Peter
Master Peter.description: Master Peter is the Cratchits' older son, who is considered for a job situation that would bring in five-and-sixpence weekly.

The Cratchit Family.name: The Cratchit Family
The Cratchit Family.description: The Cratchit Family is a family unit that celebrates Christmas together and reacts negatively to the mention of Scrooge. | The Cratchit Family is a close-knit family unit that supports each other through grief, and they share a deep love for Tiny Tim.

Peter.name: Peter
Peter.description: Peter is an individual who reacts to the lord's height by pulling up his collar, suggesting he feels self-conscious or proud. | Peter is a child in the Cratchit family, reading a book to the others.

The Spirit's Torch.name: The Spirit's Torch
The Spirit's Torch.description: The Spirit's torch emits bright sprinklings that make the family look happier at parting.

The Family.name: The Family
The Family.description: The Family is a group of people who are happy, grateful, and contented, despite being poorly dressed and having scanty clothes.

A Lost Child Travelling in the Snow.name: A Lost Child Travelling in the Snow
A Lost Child Travelling in the Snow.description: A Lost Child Travelling in the Snow is a song about a lost child in snow, sung by Tiny Tim.

The Streets.name: The Streets
The Streets.description: The Streets are the paths along which Scrooge and the Spirit walk, observing the snowy environs and the lit homes.

Lamplighter.name: Lamplighter
Lamplighter.description: The lamplighter is a person seen on the street who laughs as the Ghost passes, unaware of the Ghost's presence.

Miners.name: Miners
Miners.description: The miners are a group of people who live in the moor and work underground, and they are shown celebrating Christmas with their families.

Old Man.name: Old Man
Old Man.description: The old man is a miner who sings a Christmas song to his family, and his voice is strong when they join in the chorus.

Moor.name: Moor
Moor.description: The moor is a bleak and desert place with stones and frost, where miners live.

Sea.name: Sea
Sea.description: The sea is a location that the Ghost and Scrooge visit, characterized by thundering water and rocky caverns.

Hut.name: Hut
Hut.description: The hut is a dwelling on the moor where the miners and their families are gathered around a fire.

Lighthouse.name: Lighthouse
Lighthouse.description: A solitary lighthouse built on a reef of sunken rocks, where two men watch the light and celebrate Christmas.

Two Men (Lighthouse).name: Two Men (Lighthouse)
Two Men (Lighthouse).description: Two men who watch the lighthouse light, share a can of grog, and wish each other Merry Christmas.

Ship.name: Ship
Ship.description: A ship where the Ghost and Scrooge land, and where every man on board shares Christmas greetings and thoughts.

Scrooge's Niece.name: Scrooge's Niece
Scrooge's Niece.description: Scrooge's niece by marriage is a pretty and spirited woman who laughs heartily and expresses indignation towards Scrooge's attitude. | Scrooge's niece is Fred's wife, who, along with the others, enjoys dinner and interacts warmly with the group. | Scrooge's niece is a female relative of Scrooge who plays the harp skillfully during the family gathering, performing musical pieces that evoke memories for Scrooge. | Scrooge's niece is a woman who joins the games at the party and is seated near Scrooge and the Ghost. | Scrooge's niece by marriage is present at Fred's house and is surprised by Scrooge's arrival.

Assembled Friends.name: Assembled Friends
Assembled Friends.description: A group of friends gathered with Scrooge's nephew and niece, who laugh heartily in response to the humor.

Laughter.name: Laughter
Laughter.description: Laughter is described as irresistibly contagious and a noble adjustment in the world.

Topper.name: Topper
Topper.description: Topper is a bachelor who expresses a view on housekeeping and is attracted to one of Scrooge's niece's sisters, likely the plump one. | Topper is a participant in the family gathering, noted for his singing ability in bass, and later for his playful yet deceptive actions during blind man's-buff. | Topper is a guest at the party who engages in the game of blind man's buff and interacts with one of the plump sisters. | Topper is a guest at the party, and appears to be a familiar character who is welcomed.

Plump Sister.name: Plump Sister
Plump Sister.description: The plump sister is one of Scrooge's niece's sisters, who blushes at Topper's comment and attempts to resist laughter with aromatic vinegar. | The plump sister is a relative (likely Fred's sister) who correctly guesses that the animal thought of is Uncle Scrooge. | The plump sister is a guest at the party, and is also warmly welcomed, indicating a larger social gathering.

Plump Sister in the Lace Tucker.name: Plump Sister in the Lace Tucker
Plump Sister in the Lace Tucker.description: The plump sister in the lace tucker is a female guest at the gathering who becomes the focus of Topper's attention during the blind man's-buff game.

Harp.name: Harp
Harp.description: The harp is a musical instrument played by Scrooge's niece during the family gathering, producing a simple air that is significant to Scrooge.

The Way He Went After That Plump Sister.name: The Way He Went After That Plump Sister in the Lace Tucker
The Way He Went After That Plump Sister.description: This is an illustrative caption describing Topper's behavior towards the plump sister during the game of blind man's-buff.

Blind Man's-Buff.name: Blind Man's-Buff
Blind Man's-Buff.description: Blind man's-buff is a party game played during the gathering, in which Topper targets the plump sister with apparent deception.

The Plump Sister.name: The Plump Sister
The Plump Sister.description: The plump sister is one of the women at the party who is the target of Topper's attention during the blind man's buff.

Blind Man's Buff.name: Blind Man's Buff
Blind Man's Buff.description: Blind Man's Buff is a party game played at the gathering where one player is blindfolded and tries to catch others.

Yes and No.name: Yes and No
Yes and No.description: Yes and No is a game played at the party where one person thinks of something and others ask questions to guess it.

The Party.name: The Party
The Party.description: The party is a festive gathering with games and activities involving the characters. | The party is a celebratory gathering that brought happiness and joy, and is referred to as wonderful.

Uncle Scrooge.name: Uncle Scrooge
Uncle Scrooge.description: Uncle Scrooge is a miserly old man who is the subject of the guessing game; he is later described as becoming gay and light of heart during the vision.

London.name: London
London.description: London is the city where the animal in the guessing game lives and walks about the streets.

The Animal.name: The Animal
The Animal.description: The animal in the guessing game is a live, savage creature that growls, grunts, and talks; it is revealed to be Uncle Scrooge.

Mulled Wine.name: Mulled Wine
Mulled Wine.description: Mulled wine is a drink that Fred raises in a toast to Uncle Scrooge's health.

The Boy.name: The Boy
The Boy.description: The Boy is one of the two children brought forth by the Ghost, described as yellow, meagre, ragged, and wolfish. | A boy who is compensated by Scrooge, likely for delivering the turkey.

The Girl.name: The Girl
The Girl.description: The Girl is the other child brought forth by the Ghost, equally wretched and monstrous in appearance. | The girl is a servant in Fred's household who assists Scrooge in finding Fred.

Almshouse.name: Almshouse
Almshouse.description: An almshouse is a place of refuge for the poor, referenced as one of the places the spirit leaves his blessing.

Hospital.name: Hospital
Hospital.description: A hospital is a place for the sick, where the spirit's blessing is also left.

Gaol.name: Gaol
Gaol.description: A gaol is a jail, another refuge of misery where the spirit bestows his blessing.

Twelfth-Night.name: Twelfth-Night
Twelfth-Night.description: Twelfth-Night is a children's party they attend, after which the Ghost's aging is noticed.

Ignorance.name: Ignorance
Ignorance.description: Ignorance is a boy child shown to Scrooge, described as Man's child, and is warned against for having Doom written on his brow.

Want.name: Want
Want.description: Want is a girl child shown to Scrooge, described as Man's child, representing poverty and need.

The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come.name: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come
The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come.description: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come is a solemn Phantom, draped and hooded, that approaches Scrooge after the bell strikes twelve; it points onward but does not speak.

The City.name: The City
The City.description: The City is the urban setting toward which the Spirit points when speaking about the children Ignorance and Want. | The City is the urban setting where the Spirit leads Scrooge, springing up around them and encompassing them as they arrive.

Ghost of the Future.name: Ghost of the Future
Ghost of the Future.description: The Ghost of the Future is a silent, spectral figure shrouded in a dusky shroud, pointing ahead to guide Scrooge through the City.

Business Men.name: Business Men
Business Men.description: Business men are merchants in the City's 'Change, conversing in groups and discussing the death of an unnamed individual.

First Speaker.name: First Speaker
First Speaker.description: The first speaker is a man among Scrooge's acquaintances who discusses the deceased man's funeral and money, and later offers to attend the funeral if others do.

Red-Faced Gentleman.name: Red-Faced Gentleman
Red-Faced Gentleman.description: A red-faced gentleman with a pendulous excrescence on his nose who inquires about the deceased man's money and jokes about requiring lunch to attend the funeral.

Man with Large Chin.name: Man with Large Chin
Man with Large Chin.description: A man with a large chin who responds to the conversation, suggesting the funeral will be cheap and joking about the deceased's will.

Deceased Man.name: Deceased Man
Deceased Man.description: A man who has recently died, whose funeral and money are topics of discussion among the speakers.

First Business Man.name: First Business Man
First Business Man.description: A wealthy businessman of great importance who greets the second business man in a brief exchange.

Second Business Man.name: Second Business Man
Second Business Man.description: A wealthy businessman of great importance who responds to the first business man's greeting in a brief conversation.

Jacob.name: Jacob
Jacob.description: Scrooge's former business partner whose death is referenced in the narrative.

The Future.name: The Future
The Future.description: The temporal realm that the Spirit shows Scrooge, representing the consequences of his actions.

The Porch.name: The Porch
The Porch.description: A place where Scrooge usually stands but does not see his future self, indicating a change in his life.

The Obscure Quarter.name: The Obscure Quarter
The Obscure Quarter.description: A neglected, foul part of the town previously unknown to Scrooge, marked by crime and poverty.

The Low-Browed Shop.name: The Low-Browed Shop
The Low-Browed Shop.description: A shop dealing in scrap metal and refuse, where secrets are harbored.

Old Joe.name: Old Joe
Old Joe.description: A grey-haired man of nearly seventy years who deals in old iron and other refuse, keeping a shop with a parlour behind a screen of rags. | Old Joe is a purchaser of stolen goods who negotiates prices with the women. | Old Joe is a character involved in distributing gains from the dead man's belongings.

Charwoman.name: Charwoman
Charwoman.description: A woman who entered Old Joe's shop first with a heavy bundle, later revealed to be a charwoman.

Laundress.name: Laundress
Laundress.description: A woman who entered Old Joe's shop second with a heavy bundle, later identified as a laundress.

Undertaker's Man.name: Undertaker's Man
Undertaker's Man.description: A man in faded black who entered the shop third, startled upon seeing the women, later identified as an undertaker's man.

Old Joe's Shop.name: Old Joe's Shop
Old Joe's Shop.description: A shop dealing in old iron and refuse, containing heaps of rusty keys, nails, chains, and other junk, with a parlour behind a screen of rags.

Parlour.name: Parlour
Parlour.description: The space behind the screen of rags in Old Joe's shop where the group gathers.

Rags.name: Rags
Rags.description: Miscellaneous tatters used as a curtain and screen in Old Joe's shop.

Charcoal Stove.name: Charcoal Stove
Charcoal Stove.description: A stove made of old bricks used by Old Joe to keep warm in his shop.

The Dead Man.name: The Dead Man
The Dead Man.description: The Dead Man is the deceased individual whose belongings are being plundered, described as a wicked old screw. | The Dead Man is the deceased person whose death is central to the scene, and Scrooge wonders about his life. | The Dead Man is a person who was ill and dying, and whose death brings relief to Caroline and her husband.

The Man in Faded Black.name: The Man in Faded Black
The Man in Faded Black.description: The Man in Faded Black is a participant in the plunder who produces his plunder first.

First Woman.name: First Woman
First Woman.description: The first woman is one of the women selling items to Old Joe, including bed-curtains and a shirt.

The Corpse.name: The Corpse
The Corpse.description: The corpse is the dead man whose body is displayed on a bed, and whose life story is the focus of the scene.

The Phantom.name: The Phantom
The Phantom.description: The Phantom is a ghostly figure guiding Scrooge through the visions, pointing to the corpse's head.

The Lamp.name: The Lamp
The Lamp.description: A lamp providing light in the scene with the corpse, used by the old man.

Death.name: Death
Death.description: Death is personified as a force with dominion over the scene, but powerless over the good deeds of the dead.

Caroline's Husband.name: Caroline's Husband
Caroline's Husband.description: Caroline's Husband is a young man who brings the news of the Dead Man's death, showing a mix of relief and shame. | Caroline's husband informs her of the man's death and discusses their debt.

The Mother.name: The Mother
The Mother.description: The Mother is Caroline, who is anxious waiting for her husband and finds hope after the bad news.

The Cat.name: The Cat
The Cat.description: A cat is present in the dark, empty house, tearing at the door, contributing to the fearful atmosphere.

The Rats.name: The Rats
The Rats.description: Rats are gnawing beneath the hearthstone in the house, adding to the sense of decay and fear.

The Dark Empty House.name: The Dark Empty House
The Dark Empty House.description: A house where the Dead Man lies, described as dark and empty, with no one to mourn him.

The Lesson.name: The Lesson
The Lesson.description: The Lesson refers to the moral insight Scrooge gains from the death scene, which he vows not to forget.

Half-Drunken Woman.name: Half-Drunken Woman
Half-Drunken Woman.description: Half-Drunken Woman is a woman who informed Caroline's husband about the dead man's critical condition.

Cratchit's Wife.name: Cratchit's Wife
Cratchit's Wife.description: Cratchit's Wife is the mother of the Cratchit children, engaged in sewing and caring for the family.

The Children.name: The Children
The Children.description: The Children are the Cratchit children, who are quiet and seated around the fire.

The Debt.name: The Debt
The Debt.description: The Debt is a financial obligation owed by Caroline and her husband, which they plan to repay.

The Formerly Dark Chamber.name: The Formerly Dark Chamber
The Formerly Dark Chamber.description: The Formerly Dark Chamber is a place Scrooge was shown earlier, which he references.

Mr. Scrooge's Nephew.name: Mr. Scrooge's Nephew
Mr. Scrooge's Nephew.description: Mr. Scrooge's nephew is a kind and generous gentleman who meets Bob in the street, shows concern for his distress, and offers his help.

Churchyard.name: Churchyard
Churchyard.description: The churchyard is a graveyard where Scrooge is shown a grave, representing his potential future.

The Grave.name: The Grave
The Grave.description: The grave is a specific burial site in the churchyard that the Ghost points to, symbolizing Scrooge's potential death.

Ghost Of Christmas Present.name: Ghost Of Christmas Present
Ghost Of Christmas Present.description: The Ghost of Christmas Present is a spirit that sat in the corner of Scrooge's room during the visitation.

Christmas Time.name: Christmas Time
Christmas Time.description: Christmas Time is a holiday season that Scrooge praises and celebrates with joy and good intentions.

Bed Curtains.name: Bed Curtains
Bed Curtains.description: The bed curtains are physical objects in Scrooge's room that Scrooge holds and inspects, affirming they were not torn down.

The Gruel Saucepan.name: The Gruel Saucepan
The Gruel Saucepan.description: The gruel saucepan is a cooking vessel that Scrooge identifies in his room, part of his tangible connection to the events of the night.

The Door.name: The Door
The Door.description: The door is a physical feature in Scrooge's room through which the Ghost of Jacob Marley entered.

The Window.name: The Window
The Window.description: The window is an opening in Scrooge's room from which he saw wandering Spirits, and later opens to view the outside.

Boy.name: Boy
Boy.description: A boy in Sunday clothes who Scrooge sends to buy the turkey.

The Prize Turkey.name: The Prize Turkey
The Prize Turkey.description: The big prize turkey that Scrooge decides to buy and send to Bob Cratchit's family.

The Spirits.name: The Spirits
The Spirits.description: Supernatural beings who visited Scrooge and transformed him in one night.

The Knocker.name: The Knocker
The Knocker.description: The door knocker on Scrooge's door that he now appreciates.

The Turkey.name: The Turkey
The Turkey.description: A large turkey that Scrooge buys and sends to Camden Town, symbolizing his generosity.

The Portly Gentleman.name: The Portly Gentleman
The Portly Gentleman.description: A gentleman who visited Scrooge's counting-house the previous day and is approached by Scrooge for an apology.

Camden Town.name: Camden Town
Camden Town.description: A location in London where Scrooge sends the turkey.

The Gentleman.name: The Gentleman
The Gentleman.description: The gentleman is a collector for charity who is astonished by Scrooge's generous donation.

Dinner.name: Dinner
Dinner.description: Dinner is a specific meal that Fred arrives for, highlighting the social context of the story.

The Tank.name: The Tank
The Tank.description: The tank is the workspace area where Bob Cratchit works, and it is where Scrooge confronts him.

The Office.name: The Office
The Office.description: The office is the workplace where Scrooge and Bob Cratchit interact, significant to the plot.

Total-Abstinence Principle.name: Total-Abstinence Principle
Total-Abstinence Principle.description: The Total-Abstinence Principle is a principle that Scrooge lived upon after his transformation.
